To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the soft anomalous dimensions are expressed as sums of products of single-cusp polylogarithms in the cusp angles, and that these functions are given in terms of the logarithms of the angles, and their derivatives, through a one-dimensional representation.

the soft anomalous dimensions of Wilson lines are sums of products of logarithms and polylogarithms of the Wilson line cusp angles, and that the alphabet of polylogarithm arguments is always the same as that of the cusp angles.

MGEWs are a sum of products, each being a function of one cusp angle only, with a symbol alphabet restricted to the two cusp angles involved, and that the results of any MGEWs are expressible in terms of a basis of logarithms, powers of logarithms and polylogarithms.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the soft anomalous dimensions of non-lightlike Wilson line correlators can be written as linear combinations of products of a finite number of polylogarithmic functions, depending on a single angle.
MGEWs in non-lightlike correlators are remarkably simple, and that they can be computed with the help of a small set of building blocks, which we provide here.

, in contrast to the case of lightlike Wilson lines, MGEWs connecting non-lightlike Wilson line do not have the simple structure of a sum of products, each depending on one cusp angle only, and their symbol alphabet is not restricted to αij.
